qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: German residential rental market is subject to strict statutory rent controls (Mietspiegel, Mietpreisbremse, social housing cost caps). Lacks an economic moat and cannot earn above-inflation spreads on capital.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing: ROIC ~3.2% vs 12% hurdle, rent controls, archetype 'None', REJECT). German residential property landlord subject to statutory rent regulation (Mietspiegel, Mietpreisbremse) and sub-hurdle capital returns well below its cost of capital.
qualitative.evidence: Historical GAAP ROIC averages 3.1-3.3% against a WACC of 4.5%+. Heavy regulatory rent intervention in Germany strictly caps pricing power, while capital-intensive property ownership fails the 12% ROIC hurdle.
